sanskrit: tatas tau śakram abrūtāṃ kariṣyāvo yad icchasi tābhyāṃ ca sahitaḥ śakro vijigye daityadānavān
english: Then those two said to Indra, 'We shall do whatever you wish.' Together with them, Indra conquered the Daityas and Dānavas.

sanskrit: nara indrasya saṃgrāme hatvā śatrūn paraṃtapaḥ paulomān kālakhañjāṃś ca sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
english: Nara, the scorcher of foes, in Indra's battle, slew enemies by the hundreds of thousands — the Paulomas and the Kālakhañjas.

sanskrit: eṣa bhrānte rathe tiṣṭhan bhallenāpaharac chiraḥ jambhasya grasamānasya yajñam arjuna āhave
english: This one, Arjuna, standing on a swaying chariot, severed the head of Jambha with a broad arrow even as that demon was swallowing the sacrifice in battle.

sanskrit: eṣa pāre samudrasya hiraṇyapuram ārujat hatvā ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi nivātakavacān raṇe
english: This one shattered the golden city beyond the ocean, slaying sixty thousand Nivata-kavacas in battle.

sanskrit: eṣa devān sahendreṇa jitvā parapuraṃjayaḥ atarpayan mahābāhur arjuno jātavedasam nārāyaṇas tathaivātra bhūyaso 'nyāñ jaghāna ha
english: This great-armed Arjuna, conqueror of enemy cities, having vanquished the gods together with Indra, gratified the fire-god. And Nārāyaṇa likewise slew yet many more there.

sanskrit: evam etau mahāvīryau tau paśyata samāgatau vāsudevārjunau vīrau samavetau mahārathau
english: Thus behold these two of great valor come together — Vāsudeva and Arjuna, two heroes, two great warriors united.

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇau devau pūrvadevāv iti śrutiḥ ajeyau mānuṣe loke sendrair api surāsuraiḥ
english: These two divinities Nara and Nārāyaṇa are the primeval gods, as the scriptures declare — unconquerable in the human world even by gods and demons together with Indra.

sanskrit: eṣa nārāyaṇaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ phalgunas tu naraḥ smṛtaḥ nārāyaṇo naraś caiva sattvam ekaṃ dvidhākṛtam
english: This Kṛṣṇa is Nārāyaṇa, while Phalguna is known as Nara. Nārāyaṇa and Nara are one essence divided into two.

sanskrit: etau hi karmaṇā lokān aśnuvāte 'kṣayān dhruvān tatra tatraiva jāyete yuddhakāle punaḥ punaḥ
english: These two, through their deeds, attain imperishable and eternal worlds; they are born again and again wherever they are needed at the time of battle.

sanskrit: tasmāt karmaiva kartavyam iti hovāca nāradaḥ etad dhi sarvam ācaṣṭa vṛṣṇicakrasya vedavit
english: 'Therefore, action alone must be performed,' thus spoke Nārada. He who knows the Vedas declared all this about the wheel of the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: śaṅkhacakragadāhastaṃ yadā drakṣyasi keśavam paryādadānaṃ cāstrāṇi bhīmadhanvānam arjunam
english: When you shall behold Keśava bearing conch, discus, and mace, and Arjuna of the terrible bow taking up his weapons,

sanskrit: sanātanau mahātmānau kṛṣṇāv ekarathe sthitau duryodhana tadā tāta smartāsi vacanaṃ mama
english: the two eternal great souls, the two Kṛṣṇas standing on one chariot — then, Duryodhana my child, you shall remember my words.

sanskrit: no ced ayam abhāvaḥ syāt kurūṇāṃ pratyupasthitaḥ arthāc ca tāta dharmāc ca tava buddhir upaplutā
english: If this destruction of the Kurus were not already at hand, your mind would not be so overwhelmed against both your interest and righteousness.

sanskrit: na ced grahīṣyase vākyaṃ śrotāsi subahūn hatān tavaiva hi mataṃ sarve kuravaḥ paryupāsate
english: If you do not accept this counsel, you shall hear of very many slain. For all the Kurus attend upon your opinion alone.

sanskrit: trayāṇām eva ca mataṃ tattvam eko 'numanyate rāmeṇa caiva śaptasya karṇasya bharatarṣabha
english: Yet you alone approve as truth the counsel of only three — including Karṇa who has been cursed by Rāma as well, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: durjāteḥ sūtaputrasya śakuneḥ saubalasya ca tathā kṣudrasya pāpasya bhrātur duḥśāsanasya ca
english: The base-born son of a charioteer, Śakuni the son of Subala, and likewise your wretched, sinful brother Duḥśāsana.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca naivam āyuṣmatā vācyaṃ yan mām āttha pitāmaha kṣatradharme sthito hy asmi svadharmād anapeyivān
english: Karṇa said: 'Such words should not be spoken by you, longlived one, as you speak to me, O Grandsire. For I stand in the duty of a warrior, not having deviated from my own dharma.'

sanskrit: kiṃ cānyan mayi durvṛttaṃ yena māṃ parigarhase na hi me vṛjinaṃ kiṃ cid dhārtarāṣṭrā viduḥ kva cit
english: 'What other misconduct do you find in me for which you reproach me? The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra know no fault of mine anywhere.'

sanskrit: rājño hi dhṛtarāṣṭrasya sarvaṃ kāryaṃ priyaṃ mayā tathā duryodhanasyāpi sa hi rājye samāhitaḥ
english: 'I have always done everything pleasing to King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and likewise to Duryodhana, for he is established in the kingdom.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca karṇasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ punaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahārājam ābhāṣyedaṃ vaco 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard Karṇa's words, Bhīṣma, the son of Shantanu, again addressed the great king Dhṛtarāṣṭra with these words:

sanskrit: yad ayaṃ katthate nityaṃ hantāhaṃ pāṇḍavān iti nāyaṃ kalāpi saṃpūrṇā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: 'Though this one constantly boasts, "I shall slay the Pāṇḍavas," he is not even a fraction complete compared to the great-souled Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: anayo yo 'yam āgantā putrāṇāṃ te durātmanām tad asya karma jānīhi sūtaputrasya durmateḥ
english: 'Know the conduct of this evil-minded son of a charioteer for what it is — the ruination that is coming upon your wicked sons.'

sanskrit: enam āśritya putras te mandabuddhiḥ suyodhanaḥ avamanyata tān vīrān devaputrān ariṃdamān
english: 'Relying on this one, your slow-witted son Suyodhana has despised those heroes, the sons of gods, those tamers of foes.'

sanskrit: kiṃ cāpy anena tat karma kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ suduṣkaram tair yathā pāṇḍavaiḥ sarvair ekaikena kṛtaṃ purā
english: 'And what supremely difficult deed has this one ever done that could compare to what each one of all the Pāṇḍavas accomplished individually in the past?'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā virāṭanagare bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ priyam dhanaṃjayena vikramya kim anena tadā kṛtam
english: 'When at the city of Virāṭa he saw his dear brother slain by the valor of Dhanañjaya, what did this one do then?'

sanskrit: sahitān hi kurūn sarvān abhiyāto dhanaṃjayaḥ pramathya cācchinad gāvaḥ kim ayaṃ proṣitas tadā
english: 'When Dhanañjaya attacked all the Kurus together, routed them, and recaptured the cattle — where was this one then, gone away?'

sanskrit: gandharvair ghoṣayātrāyāṃ hriyate yat sutas tava kva tadā sūtaputro 'bhūd ya idānīṃ vṛṣāyate
english: 'When your son was being carried away by the Gandharvas during the cattle-expedition, where was this son of a charioteer who now struts about like a bull?'

sanskrit: nanu tatrāpi pārthena bhīmena ca mahātmanā yamābhyām eva cāgamya gandharvās te parājitāḥ
english: 'Was it not there too that those Gandharvas were defeated by Pārtha, by the great-souled Bhīma, and by the twins who came to the rescue?'

sanskrit: etāny asya mṛṣoktāni bahūni bharatarṣabha vikatthanasya bhadraṃ te sadā dharmārthalopinaḥ
english: 'These are the many false boasts of this man, O bull of the Bhāratas — he who is ever a braggart, ever transgressing dharma and artha. May good fortune attend you.'

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā bhāradvājo mahāmanāḥ dhṛtarāṣṭram uvācedaṃ rājamadhye 'bhipūjayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard Bhīṣma's words, the great-minded son of Bhāradvāja — Droṇa — honoring him, spoke thus to Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the midst of the kings:

sanskrit: yad āha bharataśreṣṭho bhīṣmas tat kriyatāṃ nṛpa na kāmam arthalipsūnāṃ vacanaṃ kartum arhasi
english: 'What the foremost of the Bhāratas, Bhīṣma, has said — let that be done, O king. You should not act on the word of those who are greedy for gain at the cost of desire.'

sanskrit: purā yuddhāt sādhu manye pāṇḍavaiḥ saha saṃgamam yad vākyam arjunenoktaṃ saṃjayena niveditam
english: 'Before the battle, I think it good to come to terms with the Pāṇḍavas. The words that were spoken by Arjuna and reported by Sañjaya —'

sanskrit: sarvaṃ tad abhijānāmi kariṣyati ca pāṇḍavaḥ na hy asya triṣu lokeṣu sadṛśo 'sti dhanurdharaḥ
english: 'All that I fully know, and the Pāṇḍava will do it. For there is no equal to him as an archer in all three worlds.'

sanskrit: anādṛtya tu tad vākyam arthavad droṇabhīṣmayoḥ tataḥ sa saṃjayaṃ rājā paryapṛcchata pāṇḍavam
english: But disregarding that meaningful counsel of Droṇa and Bhīṣma, the king then questioned Sañjaya about the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tadaiva kuravaḥ sarve nirāśā jīvite 'bhavan bhīṣmadroṇau yadā rājā na samyag anubhāṣate
english: From that very moment all the Kurus became hopeless of life, when the king did not properly heed Bhīṣma and Droṇa.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kim asau pāṇḍavo rājā dharmaputro 'bhyabhāṣata śrutvemā bahulāḥ senāḥ pratyarthena samāgatāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'What did that Pāṇḍava king, the son of Dharma, say upon hearing that these many armies had gathered against him?'

sanskrit: kim icchaty abhisaṃrambhād yotsyamāno yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kasya svid bhrātṛputrāṇāṃ cintāsu mukham īkṣate
english: 'What does Yudhiṣṭhira seek, preparing to fight with passion? Upon whose face among his brothers and sons does he look in deliberation?'

sanskrit: ke svid enaṃ vārayanti śāmya yudhyeti vā punaḥ nikṛtyā kopitaṃ mandair dharmajñaṃ dharmacāriṇam
english: 'Who dissuade him saying "make peace," and who urge "fight"? Who, by treacherous means, have angered this knower of dharma, this follower of righteousness?'

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rājño mukham udīkṣante pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha yudhiṣṭhirasya bhadraṃ te sa sarvān anuśāsti ca
english: Sañjaya said: 'The Pāñcālas along with the Pāṇḍavas look to the face of King Yudhiṣṭhira — may good fortune be yours — and he commands them all.'

sanskrit: pṛthagbhūtāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajāḥ āyāntam abhinandanti kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: 'The chariot-hosts of the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas, assembled separately, welcome Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, as he approaches.'

sanskrit: tamaḥ sūryam ivodyantaṃ kaunteyaṃ dīptatejasam pāñcālāḥ pratinandanti tejorāśim ivodyatam
english: 'The Pāñcālas welcome the son of Kuntī blazing with splendor as though the sun rising from darkness, like a rising mass of radiance.'

sanskrit: ā gopālāvipālebhyo nandamānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram pāñcālāḥ kekayā matsyāḥ pratinandanti pāṇḍavam
english: 'From the cowherds and shepherds upward, all rejoice in Yudhiṣṭhira; the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, and the Matsyas welcome the Pāṇḍava.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyo rājaputryaś ca viśāṃ duhitaraś ca yāḥ krīḍantyo 'bhisamāyānti pārthaṃ saṃnaddham īkṣitum
english: 'Brahmin women, princesses, and the daughters of the merchant class come out at play to see Pārtha arrayed for battle.'

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca saṃjayācakṣva kenāsmān pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata dhṛṣṭadyumnena senānyā somakāḥ kiṃbalā iva
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'Tell me, Sañjaya, with whom have the Pāṇḍavas engaged against us? The Somakas with Dhṛṣṭadyumna as their general — like what?'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gāvalgaṇis tu tat pṛṣṭaḥ sabhāyāṃ kurusaṃsadi niḥśvasya subhṛśaṃ dīrghaṃ muhuḥ saṃcintayann iva tatrānimittato daivāt sūtaṃ kaśmalam āviśat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Gavalgaṇa's son, questioned thus in the assembly of the Kurus, heaved a long and heavy sigh, seeming to reflect again and again; then, for no apparent reason, by the force of fate, a swoon came over the charioteer.

sanskrit: tadācacakṣe puruṣaḥ sabhāyāṃ rājasaṃsadi saṃjayo 'yaṃ mahārāja mūrcchitaḥ patito bhuvi vācaṃ na sṛjate kāṃ cid dhīnaprajño 'lpacetanaḥ
english: Then a man declared in the royal assembly: 'O great king, this Sañjaya has fainted and fallen to the ground; he utters no words, his awareness diminished, his consciousness faint.'

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca apaśyat saṃjayo nūnaṃ kuntīputrān mahārathān tair asya puruṣavyāghrair bhṛśam udvejitaṃ manaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'Sañjaya must have beheld the great chariot-warriors who are the sons of Kuntī; his mind has been greatly agitated by those tiger-like men.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saṃjayaś cetanāṃ labdhvā pratyāśvasyedam abravīt dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahārāja sabhāyāṃ kurusaṃsadi
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Sañjaya, having regained consciousness and composure, said this to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O great king, in the assembly of the Kurus:

sanskrit: dṛṣṭavān asmi rājendra kuntīputrān mahārathān matsyarājagṛhāvāsād avarodhena karśitān śṛṇu yair hi mahārāja pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'I have seen, O king of kings, the great chariot-warriors who are the sons of Kuntī, emaciated from their confinement during their stay in the house of the Matsya king. Listen, O great king, to those with whom the Pāṇḍavas have engaged.'

sanskrit: yo naiva roṣān na bhayān na kāmān nārthakāraṇāt na hetuvādād dharmātmā satyaṃ jahyāt kathaṃ cana
english: 'He who, for the sake of neither anger, nor fear, nor desire, nor material gain, nor logical argument, would ever abandon truth — the righteous-souled one —'

sanskrit: yaḥ pramāṇaṃ mahārāja dharme dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ajātaśatruṇā tena pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'He who is the standard in righteousness, O great king — the foremost among upholders of dharma — by that Ajātaśatru, the Pāṇḍavas have engaged.'

sanskrit: yasya bāhubale tulyaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nāsti kaś cana yo vai sarvān mahīpālān vaśe cakre dhanurdharaḥ tena vo bhīmasenena pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'He who has no equal on earth in the strength of his arms, that bowman who brought all kings under his sway — by that Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍavas have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: niḥsṛtānāṃ jatugṛhād dhiḍimbāt puruṣādakāt ya eṣām abhavad dvīpaḥ kuntīputro vṛkodaraḥ
english: 'When they escaped from the house of lac and from Hiḍimba, the man-eater, he who became their refuge — Vṛkodara, the son of Kuntī —'

sanskrit: yājñasenīm atho yatra sindhurājo 'pakṛṣṭavān tatraiṣām abhavad dvīpaḥ kuntīputro vṛkodaraḥ
english: 'And where the king of the Sindhus dragged away Yājñasenī, there too he became their refuge — Vṛkodara, the son of Kuntī.'

sanskrit: yaś ca tān saṃgatān sarvān pāṇḍavān vāraṇāvate dahyato mocayām āsa tena vas te 'bhyayuñjata
english: 'And he who freed all the Pāṇḍavas assembled together while burning at Vāraṇāvata — by him they have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāyāś caratā prītiṃ yena krodhavaśā hatāḥ praviśya viṣamaṃ ghoraṃ parvataṃ gandhamādanam
english: 'By whom, to bring delight to Kṛṣṇa, those demons overcome by rage were slain, having entered the terrible and impassable mountain Gandhamādana —'

sanskrit: yasya nāgāyutaṃ vīryaṃ bhujayoḥ sāram arpitam tena vo bhīmasenena pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'He whose strength equal to ten thousand elephants is concentrated in the essence of his arms — by that Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍavas have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvitīyo vikramya tuṣṭyarthaṃ jātavedasaḥ ajayad yaḥ purā vīro yudhyamānaṃ puraṃdaram
english: 'The hero who, with Kṛṣṇa as his second, once conquered Indra himself who was fighting him, in order to gratify the fire-god —'

sanskrit: yaḥ sa sākṣān mahādevaṃ giriśaṃ śūlapāṇinam toṣayām āsa yuddhena devadevam umāpatim
english: 'He who gratified the great god himself, Giresha, the trident-bearer, the god of gods, the husband of Umā, by combat —'

sanskrit: yaś ca sarvān vaśe cakre lokapālān dhanurdharaḥ tena vo vijayenājau pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'That bowman who brought all the world-guardians under his sway — by that Vijaya in battle the Pāṇḍavas have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: yaḥ pratīcīṃ diśaṃ cakre vaśe mlecchagaṇāyutām sa tatra nakulo yoddhā citrayodhī vyavasthitaḥ
english: 'He who brought the western quarter under his sway together with its multitudes of barbarians — that Nakula, a fighter of varied combat, stands there as warrior.'

sanskrit: tena vo darśanīyena vīreṇātidhanurbhṛtā mādrīputreṇa kauravya pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'By that handsome hero, that supreme bowman, the son of Mādrī, O Kauravya, the Pāṇḍavas have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: yaḥ kāśīn aṅgamagadhān kaliṅgāṃś ca yudhājayat tena vaḥ sahadevena pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'He who conquered by battle the Kāśis, the Aṅgas, the Māgadhas, and the Kaliṅgas — by that Sahadeva the Pāṇḍavas have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: yasya vīryeṇa sadṛśāś catvāro bhuvi mānavāḥ aśvatthāmā dhṛṣṭaketuḥ pradyumno rukmir eva ca
english: 'Those who equal him in valor are only four men on earth: Aśvatthāmā, Dhṛṣṭaketu, Pradyumna, and Rukmin.'

sanskrit: tena vaḥ sahadevena pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata yavīyasā nṛvīreṇa mādrīnandikareṇa ca
english: 'By that Sahadeva, the younger, the hero among men, the joy of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: tapaś cacāra yā ghoraṃ kāśikanyā purā satī bhīṣmasya vadham icchantī pretyāpi bharatarṣabha
english: 'She who was the virtuous princess of Kāśi and performed terrible austerities of old, even after death wishing for the slaying of Bhīṣma, O bull of the Bhāratas —'

sanskrit: pāñcālasya sutā jajñe daivāc ca sa punaḥ pumān strīpuṃsoḥ puruṣavyāghra yaḥ sa veda guṇāguṇān
english: 'She was born as the daughter of the Pāñcāla king, and by fate he was born again as a male — that tiger among men who knows the qualities and defects of both woman and man.'

sanskrit: yaḥ kaliṅgān samāpede pāñcālo yuddhadurmadaḥ śikhaṇḍinā vaḥ kuravaḥ kṛtāstreṇābhyayuñjata
english: 'By Śikhaṇḍī, that Pāñcāla, maddened for battle, who attacked the Kaliṅgas, trained in arms, you Kurus have been engaged.'

sanskrit: yāṃ yakṣaḥ puruṣaṃ cakre bhīṣmasya nidhane kila maheṣvāsena raudreṇa pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'The one whom a yaksha made into a man — for the purpose of slaying Bhīṣma, it is said — by that great bowman of fierce power the Pāṇḍavas have engaged.'

sanskrit: maheṣvāsā rājaputrā bhrātaraḥ pañca kekayāḥ sumṛṣṭakavacāḥ śūrās taiś ca vas te 'bhyayuñjata
english: 'The great bowmen, the five royal brothers of Kekaya, their armor well-polished, those heroes — by them too they have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: yo dīrghabāhuḥ kṣiprāstro dhṛtimān satyavikramaḥ tena vo vṛṣṇivīreṇa yuyudhānena saṃgaraḥ
english: 'He who is long-armed, swift with weapons, steadfast, truly valiant — by that hero of the Vṛṣṇis, Yuyudhāna, battle has been engaged against you.'

sanskrit: ya āsīc charaṇaṃ kāle pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām raṇe tena virāṭena pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'He who was a refuge for the great-souled Pāṇḍavas at the time of need — by that Virāṭa in battle the Pāṇḍavas have engaged.'

sanskrit: yaḥ sa kāśipatī rājā vārāṇasyāṃ mahārathaḥ sa teṣām abhavad yoddhā tena vas te 'bhyayuñjata
english: 'He who is the lord of Kāśi, the king, the great chariot-warrior of Vārāṇasī — he became their fighter; by him they have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: śiśubhir durjayaiḥ saṃkhye draupadeyair mahātmabhiḥ āśīviṣasamasparśaiḥ pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'By the young sons of Draupadī, difficult to conquer in battle, great-souled, whose touch is like that of a venomous serpent — by them the Pāṇḍavas have engaged.'

sanskrit: yaḥ kṛṣṇasadṛśo vīrye yudhiṣṭhirasamo dame tenābhimanyunā saṃkhye pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'He who equals Kṛṣṇa in valor and Yudhiṣṭhira in self-restraint — by that Abhimanyu in battle the Pāṇḍavas have engaged.'

sanskrit: yaś caivāpratimo vīrye dhṛṣṭaketur mahāyaśāḥ duḥsahaḥ samare kruddhaḥ śaiśupālir mahārathaḥ tena vaś cedirājena pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'And he who is matchless in valor, Dhṛṣṭaketu of great fame, unbearable when angry in battle, the great chariot-warrior son of Śiśupāla — by that king of the Cedis the Pāṇḍavas have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: yaḥ saṃśrayaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ devānām iva vāsavaḥ tena vo vāsudevena pāṇḍavā abhyayuñjata
english: 'He who is the refuge of the Pāṇḍavas as Vāsava is the refuge of the gods — by that Vāsudeva the Pāṇḍavas have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: tathā cedipater bhrātā śarabho bharatarṣabha karakarṣeṇa sahitas tābhyāṃ vas te 'bhyayuñjata
english: 'Likewise the brother of the Cedi king, Śarabha, O bull of the Bhāratas, together with Karakarṣa — by those two they have engaged against you.'

sanskrit: jārāsaṃdhiḥ sahadevo jayatsenaś ca tāv ubhau drupadaś ca mahātejā balena mahatā vṛtaḥ tyaktātmā pāṇḍavārthāya yotsyamāno vyavasthitaḥ
english: 'Jarāsandha's son Sahadeva, and Jayadratha — both of them — and Drupada of great splendor, surrounded by a great force, having dedicated himself, stands ready to fight for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ prācyodīcyā mahīkṣitaḥ śataśo yān apāśritya dharmarājo vyavasthitaḥ
english: 'These and many others — kings of the east and the north — hundreds of them, relying upon whom the king of righteousness stands arrayed.'
